business_problem: Virgin Money needed to reduce contact-center demand and improve digital self-service because credit-card customers often called for help instead of completing questions and account updates inside the mobile app.
solution_summary: Virgin Money and IBM Consulting built Redi, an AI-powered banking assistant, on a Microsoft conversational stack hosted in Virgin Money's private cloud. Power Virtual Agents and Bot Framework Composer provide the core digital host, while natural-language understanding and API integrations let customers ask questions, complete account tasks, and receive proactive messages inside the credit-card app. The bank and IBM designed the rollout in phases so the same platform could begin with credit cards and later extend to current-account support as part of a multi-product virtual-assistant strategy. Redi now supports more than 100 credit-card queries, handles end-to-end account updates such as credit-limit increases, and integrates with over 50 back-end API calls to tailor support. The result is a reusable conversational-banking platform that sits inside the app rather than forcing customers to leave for a phone call or separate channel.

solution_components.name: Power Virtual Agents
solution_components.role: Provides the conversational host for Redi's banking assistant experience.

solution_components.name: Bot Framework Composer
solution_components.role: Supports the virtual assistant workflows and orchestration behind Redi's customer journeys.

data_flow: Customer questions flow from the credit-card mobile app into Redi, the conversational stack interprets the request, more than 50 APIs call Virgin Money's back-end systems to retrieve or update account data, and proactive messages can be pushed back into the app as account events occur.
business_outcome: Virgin Money increased customer engagement and self-service, improved satisfaction, and created a reusable conversational-banking platform it is extending across multiple product lines.
